newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bouygues, Veba in telecom deal.
newsitem.headline: Bouygues, Veba in telecom deal.

text.p: French construction and media group Bouygues said on Tuesday it was cementing a telecoms cooperation deal with Germany's VEBA by setting up joint-venture companies.
The deals also involve Italy's STET. Bouygues has had a joint-venture with STET called BS Telecom since December 1996.

BS Telecom will take a 80 percent stake in holding company BSV while VEBA will have 20 percent. This company will have an operating subsidiary BSV Residentiel to offer fixed telecommunications services in France from 1998 to households and small and medium sized companies.
BS Entreprises, a 51 percent unti of BS Telecom, will offer services to companies.
BSV, which will rival both France Telecom and Cegetel in France, will "define its strategy and decide on the necessary investments," Bouygues said.
Cegetel counts Generale des Eaux, BT, SBC and Mannesmann as its backers.
Veba since 1994 has had a 17.5 percent stake in Bouygues Telecom, which operates France's third digital mobile telecommunications service.
STET, for its part, has a 19.6 percent stake in BDT which owns 55 percent of Bouygues Telecom. Other shareholders are banks Paribas and BNP Banexi as well as privately-owned Decaux.
